Name: Blue-Green Deployment
Strategy: Maintain two identical environments; switch traffic atomically via load balancer/DNS
Risk: Low — instant rollback by switching back to old environment
Blast Radius: Full environment — all users switch at once
Tooling: AWS CodeDeploy; Kubernetes Ingress; HAProxy; Nginx
Gotcha: Requires 2x infrastructure during deployment; database schema must be backward compatible

Name: Canary Deployment
Strategy: Route a small percentage of traffic to new version; monitor; gradually increase
Risk: Low — small blast radius; automated rollback on metric degradation
Tooling: Argo Rollouts; Flagger; AWS AppMesh; Istio; LaunchDarkly
Gotcha: Canary metrics need statistical significance — 1% traffic may not surface rare bugs; need sufficient soak time

Name: Rolling Update
Strategy: Replace instances one at a time (or in batches); old and new versions coexist briefly
Risk: Medium — partial rollout means mixed versions serving traffic
Rollback Time: Minutes to hours (depends on fleet size)
Tooling: Kubernetes default; AWS ECS; Systemd; Ansible
Gotcha: Mixed-version window can cause issues if API contracts change; ensure backward/forward compatibility

Name: Feature Flags
Strategy: Wrap new code in feature flags; enable per-user/percentage/segment without deploying
Risk: Very Low — disable flag instantly without deployment
Tooling: LaunchDarkly; Unleash; Flagsmith; Split; ConfigCat; custom
Gotcha: Feature flag debt accumulates fast — schedule cleanup; stale flags become permanent complexity

Name: Dark Launch
Strategy: Deploy new code path but don't expose to users; compare outputs with production path
Risk: Very Low — new path not serving users; only shadow traffic
Gotcha: Shadow traffic doubles load on downstream dependencies — use sampling for expensive operations

Name: A/B Testing Release
Strategy: Route users to different versions based on experiment configuration; measure business metrics
Risk: Low — experiment groups are controlled and monitored
Gotcha: Statistical significance requires sufficient sample size and duration — don't call experiments early

Name: Recreate Deployment
Strategy: Stop all old instances; deploy new instances; accept downtime
Risk: High — full downtime during deployment; no rollback without redeployment
Blast Radius: All users — complete outage during deploy
Tooling: Basic CI/CD; scripts; Kubernetes Recreate strategy
Gotcha: Only acceptable for non-production environments or scheduled maintenance windows

Name: GitOps
Strategy: Git repository is the source of truth for desired state; automated sync to cluster
Risk: Low — revert git commit to rollback; audit trail built in
Blast Radius: Depends on deployment strategy used by GitOps controller
Gotcha: Drift detection is critical — manual changes to cluster should be prevented or detected and reverted

Name: Progressive Delivery
Strategy: Combine canary + feature flags + automated analysis for fully automated safe releases
Risk: Very Low — multi-layered safety with automated rollback
Blast Radius: Starts small; expands based on metrics
Tooling: Argo Rollouts + Prometheus; Flagger + Istio; Spinnaker
Gotcha: Requires mature observability — automated analysis is only as good as your metrics and SLOs

Name: Ring-Based Deployment
Strategy: Deploy to concentric rings: internal → dogfood → early adopters → all users
Risk: Low — each ring gates the next; issues caught in smaller rings first
Gotcha: Ring promotion criteria must be automated — manual gates slow down releases and create bottlenecks

Name: Immutable Infrastructure
Strategy: Never modify running infrastructure; always deploy fresh instances from versioned artifacts
Risk: Low — old artifact is always available for rollback
Gotcha: Configuration drift is eliminated but debugging live issues is harder — no SSH to fix in place

Name: Database Migration Safety
Strategy: Separate database migrations from application deployments; expand-contract pattern
Risk: Medium — schema changes are the hardest to rollback
Rollback Time: Hours to days for data migrations
Blast Radius: All users if schema change is backward-incompatible
Tooling: Flyway; Liquibase; Alembic; Atlas; prisma migrate
Gotcha: Never deploy a backward-incompatible schema change and new code in the same release

Name: Rollback Strategy
Strategy: Pre-planned rollback procedure for every deployment; tested and documented
Risk: Depends on strategy — instant for flags; minutes for blue-green; hours for data migrations
Tooling: Deployment tooling rollback commands; runbook automation
Gotcha: Rollback must be tested — an untested rollback plan is not a plan; include database rollback scripts

Name: Deployment Freeze
Strategy: No deployments during high-traffic periods or critical business events
Risk: Low — prevents deployment-caused incidents during critical windows
Tooling: Calendar blocks; CI/CD gate rules; PagerDuty integration
Gotcha: Freeze windows accumulate deployment pressure — keep them short and schedule catch-up releases

Name: Release Train
Strategy: Fixed-cadence release schedule (e.g. weekly/biweekly); all features ready by cutoff ship together
Tooling: CI/CD with branch-based releases; feature branches
Gotcha: Late features that miss the train create pressure to skip testing — enforce the cutoff strictly
